statement.text:
Construct a characteristic subgroup N of a finitely generated free group
F such that F/N is infinite and simple. If no such exists, it would follow that
d(S 2 ) = d(S) for every infinite finitely generated simple group S. There is reason to
believe that this is false.                                                  J. Wiegold
  ∗ It is proved that for all n ⩾ 2, the free group F admits continuum many pairwise
                                                     n
non-isomorphic infinite simple characteristic quotients (R. Coulon, F. Fournier-Facio,
https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.11684).
